reviewed_by: Gemini Pro blind reviewer, batch G1-MG-Q4-Harden v2 (mat_g1_mg_q4_1, mat_g1_mg_q4_3, mat_g1_mg_q4_4), 2026-08-18

competency_fulfillment.rationale: The generated questions successfully fulfill the competency by asking students to solve problems involving various time units specified: hour ("lasts for 1 hour"), half hour ("lasts half an hour (30 minutes)"), quarter hour ("lasts a quarter of an hour (15 minutes)"), days in a week ("What day of the week is May 21?"), and months in a year ("How many months later is the exhibit?").

comprehensive_coverage.rationale: All required time concepts outlined in the competency are covered. The packet includes elapsed time in hours ("How many hours did Sam spend?"), elapsed time in minutes mapped to half hours ("How many minutes did it last?"), end times from start times ("What time does it end?"), reading days of the week ("What day of the week is June 6?"), and counting months ("What month will it be in 2 months?").

cognitive_capacity.rationale: The difficulty is well-calibrated for Grade 1 Quarter 4. Calculating the end time when adding 1 hour, 30 minutes, or 15 minutes is kept simple without complex hour-rollovers (e.g., "starts at 9:00 and lasts a quarter of an hour (15 minutes)"). Counting months is limited to small, easily manageable numbers (e.g., "in 2 months", "How many months later").

variant_comprehensiveness.rationale: The problem variants provide a good mix of question styles. There are forward-counting time additions ("starts at 8:00 and lasts for 1 hour. What time does it end?"), duration calculations ("began at 11:00 and finished at 11:30. How many minutes did it last?"), forward-counting months ("This month is March. What month will it be in 2 months?"), and calendar day retrieval ("Look at the May 2025 calendar. What day of the week is May 21?").

competency_alignment.rationale: The terminology and concepts strictly align with the competency text. The scaffolding included in the prompt, such as "half an hour (30 minutes)" and "quarter of an hour (15 minutes)", bridges the gap between conversational fractional hours and minute calculations safely for Grade 1 without overstepping bounds.

scale_appropriateness.rationale: The parameters and number ranges scale logically. Time intervals revolve around neat, whole units, half units, or quarters starting from top-of-the-hour times (e.g., 9:00, 10:00, 8:00). Month additions range reasonably from 2 to 4 months, which allows students to use finger-counting or basic mental math without strain.
